heading: Choosing an Anarkali suit

p: An Anarkali is a long, flared kurta – usually floor or calf length – worn with fitted pants and a dupatta. An Anarkali gown is a one-piece version, often worn with just a dupatta. Both are the easiest festive outfits for weddings, Diwali and Eid because they look dressy yet let you sit, dance and move freely. All Anarkalis here are made in our own unit in Jaipur, in sizes XS–3XL (4XL in linen & velvet styles) or stitched to your measurements for free.

list: Georgette and chiffon: light and flowing – sangeet, mehndi, summer weddings.
Taffeta silk with gota work: a soft sheen for evening functions and receptions.
Velvet: rich and warm for winter weddings, Diwali and Christmas abroad.
Cotton: breathable for day events, pujas and haldi.

p: A suit set (kurta, pants and dupatta) is the most versatile – you can re-style the kurta with other bottoms. A gown is quicker to wear and looks seamless in photos. Floor-length styles look dressiest; calf-length ones are easier to dance in.

Anarkalis are fitted at the bust and flared below, so the bust measurement matters most. Use our size converter or choose free custom fit – and tell us your height if you want a specific length. Tall? See our guide to Indian wedding outfits for tall women.

faq: What is the difference between an Anarkali suit and an Anarkali gown?
An Anarkali suit is a flared kurta worn with pants and a dupatta; an Anarkali gown is a one-piece flared dress, usually worn with a dupatta.
Is an Anarkali good for a wedding guest?
Yes – it is one of the most popular wedding guest outfits because it looks festive and stays comfortable through long functions and dancing.
Which Anarkali fabric is best for winter weddings?
Velvet is the warmest and richest choice; taffeta silk with a shawl also works for cool evenings.
Can I get an Anarkali in my exact size?
Yes. Choose a ready size from XS to 3XL (4XL in linen & velvet styles) or free custom fit – we stitch it to your bust, waist, hip and length.
